# Mixcōātl and the industries that were always telling its story
Archetypes are not metaphors; they are job descriptions written early. **Mixcōātl**'s was unusually clear.

Mixcōātl's myths are the Aztec origin-story in one figure: the wilderness god who taught the city-builders how to hunt, and whose star-road they followed south.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Mixcōātl
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Clouds, Hunting, the Milky Way
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Technology & Innovation · Energy & Natural World · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 154 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Serpent of Stars.** The Chichimec tribes who became the Aztec nobility followed his road: the Milky Way, which the Nahuatl called Mixcōātl, the Cloud Serpent, slithering nightly across the sky.  The migrating peoples read their path in his body — the desert crossed by the serpent's light — and when they founded Tenochtitlan, they enthroned the wilderness-guide among the city's great gods, the god of where they had come from. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Bow of the Chichimecs.** As Camaxtle, he gave the wandering tribes the bow and the fire-drill — the two technologies of the road.  The Aztec coronation rites remembered: the new Tlatoani dressed as Mixcōātl for the warrior's investiture, and the festival of Quecholli ("the precious feather") honored him with the hunt's own weapons laid on his altar — the city's annual thanks to the god who fed it before it had fields. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science

*Space agencies, astronomy, and the orbital economy. (Sector: Technology & Innovation)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The Milky Way as his body; the star-road personified.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Environmental & Climate Services

*Climate science, ecology, and sustainability consulting. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The cloud-serpent; weather as a living road.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Sports, Fitness & Competition

*Athletics, fitness brands, and competitive leagues. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*The hunt; the oldest competitive pursuit.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Mixcōātl performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Mixcōātl's myths are the Aztec origin-story in one figure: the wilderness god who taught the city-builders how to hunt, and whose star-road they followed south. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in space, astronomy & celestial science, environmental & climate services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/mixcoatl/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
